citation.title: Populating cellular metamaterials on the extrema of attainable elasticity through neuroevolution
citation.authors: Maohua Yan, Ruicheng Wang, Ke Liu
citation.venue: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 440 (2025) 117950 (version of record per Crossref, not accessed); coded from arXiv (cs.NE; also cs.CE)
citation.version_coded: arXiv v4 (13 Mar 2025; v1 15 Dec 2024), PDF; version of record not open access per Crossref licence metadata, not accessed

included.reason: I-SPEED (screening code confirmed at full text; qualitative primary outcome, no classical method run)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Qualitative: gradient-based TO is said to be inefficient for surveying the metamaterial design space and unable to reveal attainable property bounds, whereas CPPN neuroevolution efficiently finds Pareto-front designs; no TO is run and no cost is compared.
claim.key_phrase: they are not efficient tools for surveying the vast design space of metamaterials
claim.location: Abstract (§5.1 rule 3: no quantitative classical comparison anywhere); related qualitative statements in Sec. 3.3 and 3.5
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not derivable: no runtime, no FE-evaluation count comparison and no classical run are reported. The method evolves a population of 500 for 800 generations per study on 256 CPU processors (Sec. 3); its runtime is not stated.
claim.alternatives: (1) Sec. 3.3 (qualitative quality and coverage): after 800 iterations the three orthotropic trade-offs are consistent with Ref. [5], and unlike TO-driven methods, which give sparse Pareto points, the method fills the front densely and uniformly; Ref. [5] as printed is Babaee et al. 2013 (Adv. Mater.), and no Ref. [5] data appear in Fig. 11. (2) Sec. 3.5 (qualitative cost): collecting all evaluated designs into a database wastes no computation, unlike TO, which produces one design at a time. (3) Introduction (other methods, not this article's result): VAE generation is described as thousands of times faster than traditional TO.

baseline.classical_method: Gradient-based TO for metamaterial design (density-based, level-set and phase-field methods named in the Introduction); not run. Sec. 3.3 compares qualitatively with results reported in Ref. [5]
baseline.implementation: not applicable (no classical run). ML side: custom NEAT-style CPPN neuroevolution with RVEA reference-vector selection and constraint-violation ranking; FE homogenization on Delaunay triangle meshes (Sec. 2, App. A); software not stated
baseline.hardware_ml: Alibaba Cloud machines with AMD EPYC 7H12 64-core processors, 256 processors in total, 2.60 GHz, 503 GiB RAM; no GPU (Sec. 3)
baseline.problem_size: 2D periodic unit cells: a 35×35 point cloud on the symmetry patch, mapped by symmetry and meshed with Delaunay triangles (Sec. 2.1.3, 3); FE element count not stated
baseline.classical_iterations: not applicable; the neuroevolution uses population 500 and 800 generations per study (Sec. 3)
baseline.training_time: not applicable (no offline training; CPPNs are evolved per study from random networks, Sec. 1, 2)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not applicable (data-free); the 486,852 evaluated designs form a by-product database (Sec. 2.1.1, 3.5)
baseline.quality_metric: FE-homogenized effective properties (average E and ν from compliance-tensor components; C11, C12, C22, C33, C13) and Pareto-front coverage, shown in plots (Figs. 8-12, App. A)
baseline.quality_gap: not quantified; no classical designs are evaluated. Examples: isotropic unit cell 1 has E = 0.0001 and ν = -0.8621; unit cell 6 has E = 0.0011 and ν = 0.9790 (Sec. 3.1)

R1.evidence: Abstract, Sec. 3.3 and 3.5: the efficiency claim against gradient-based TO is backed by no TO run, runtime, FE-evaluation count or matched-quality comparison. The only link to TO results is the qualitative statement that the orthotropic Pareto fronts are consistent with Ref. [5] and denser than TO-driven results (Sec. 3.3); Fig. 11 shows no Ref. [5] data [checked PDF p. 31].

R2.evidence: No classical optimization is run (Sec. 3), so the comparator's implementation, solver and hardware cannot be assessed; the claim about TO rests on the literature (Introduction; Ref. [5] in Sec. 3.3). Unsure, so pass.

R3.evidence: CPPNs are evolved per study from random initial networks without prior data or offline training (Sec. 1 aim; Sec. 2; Conclusion), so there is no training or data cost to amortize; the evolutionary cost (population 500, 800 generations, Sec. 3; runtime not reported) belongs under R1/R2.

R4.evidence: Sec. 2 (Fig. 1b, Alg. 1) and App. A: every candidate's properties come from FE homogenization of the meshed design. Designs with interior or exterior discontinuity stay in the population and are ranked by a constraint-violation measure (Sec. 2.2.3, Fig. 6), but the share of infeasible designs in the final Pareto sets and in the 486,852-design database (Sec. 2.1.1) is not reported. No mesh-convergence check is reported for the 35×35 point-cloud meshes. Representative designs are chosen as distinct extreme combinations (Sec. 3.2).

reporting.n_test_cases: 5 design studies: isotropic p31m (E-ν), tetragonal p4mm and p4 (E-ν), orthotropic p2mm (3 modulus pairs), fully anisotropic p1 (C12-C13); one run each, no repeats reported (Sec. 3.1-3.4)

notes: Inclusion and stratum are judgment calls. The article never runs a classical optimizer and reports no runtime, no FE-evaluation count comparison and no quantitative quality comparison with TO. The primary outcome is the abstract's qualitative efficiency claim (§5.1 rule 3), so the record enters stratum speed with R1 = fail. If the verifier requires an executed or quantified classical comparison, the record becomes FT-NOCOMPARISON; if Sec. 3.3 (consistency with Ref. [5], denser Pareto coverage) is taken as the primary outcome, it becomes stratum Q. Ref. [5] as printed (Babaee et al. 2013, '3D Soft Metamaterials with Negative Poisson's Ratio') is cited as a TO-driven method, which its title does not suggest; the citation may be mis-numbered [inferred]. Method family neural_reparam: CPPNs are neural networks whose weights and topology are evolved per study without data (the screening code agreed). Evaluation budget: if each generation evaluates 500 offspring, one study uses about 4×10⁵ FE homogenizations [inferred from Sec. 3; the offspring count per generation is not stated]; the text reports 486,852 stored samples in total (Sec. 2.1.1). Reporting locators: hardware and settings = Sec. 3; constraints = Sec. 2.2.3; data statement = Data availability section (on request); no code statement. retest_candidate false: no public code and no classical speed claim to re-test. Coded arXiv v4; the CMAME version of record (doi from Crossref) was not accessed. Screening code was I-SPEED.
